correctness.rationale: The fixed icosahedral graph has 12 vertices, 30 graph edges; the matching complex is the independence complex of its line graph. Independent code enumerated full (5887 faces), one-edge-deleted (5115), and endpoint-removed link (771) complexes with f-vectors (30,315,1400,2535,1482,125), (29,294,1260,2197,1235,100), and (21,140,338,247,25). It constructed and verified acyclic Morse matchings with 2850/2495/374 pairs and critical cells (1,0,0,125,61,0)/(1,0,0,96,28,0)/(1,0,9,13,0,0). An independent second exact checker reconstructed the signed integer Morse boundaries, rational/modular ranks, and selected 61x61,28x28,7x7 integer minor determinants −3,1,−1; whole rank mod3 drops from 61 to 60, giving exactly Z/3 among homology, while deletion and link have unit Smith invariants. With the one-vertex critical 0-cell and positive-dimensional two-level CW cells, unimodular changes yield wedge-plus-Moore decomposition of parent, 68 S3 for deletion, and 2 S2+6 S3 for link. The deletion–link cofiber long exact sequence injects Z6 into Z68 with quotient torsion exactly Z/3, hence index three. Icosahedron graph automorphism group is edge-transitive (120 automorphisms, edge orbit 30 as coded). This is fixed finite exhaustion, not a sample extrapolated to larger graphs.

evidence: Outerplanar graph sphere-wedge theorem cannot apply: I-e has 12 vertices and 29 edges > 2*12−3=21. Classical torsion results for complete graph and chessboard matching complexes concern different graph families.

originality.rationale: The published icosahedral matching-complex 3-torsion counterexample gives the parent homotopy type, explicitly prior here. The new claims are homotopy after removal of ANY graph edge, endpoint-removed link and primitive saturation defect in connecting map. Prior edge-deletion splittings for other graphs or outerplanar wedge theorem do not imply this 29-edge nonouterplanar example.
